rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes increasing Al to ~10 at.% in an AlNbTiZr medium-entropy alloy coating, while the paper systematically varied Al (0–25 at.%) in an AlTiCrZrNbTa high-entropy alloy coating. Both involve Al addition to a multi-principal-element coating, but the base alloy systems differ (NbTiZr vs. TiCrZrNbTa), making it a different specific lever.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies high-temperature steam oxidation at 800–1600 °C for LOCA simulation, while the paper used isothermal oxidation in flowing steam at 1000 °C (60 min) and 1100 °C (30 min). Both are high-temperature steam oxidation, but the hypothesis covers a broader temperature range without the paper's specific time and flow conditions.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes formation of a dense protective oxide scale (Nb2Zr6O17 and ZrO2) as a diffusion barrier. The paper's mechanism involves a composite Al2O3-TiO2-Cr2O3 layer suppressing oxygen diffusion, with excess Al causing intermetallics and oxide discontinuity. Both are protective oxide barrier mechanisms, but the specific oxide phases and the role of Al in disrupting vs. forming the barrier differ substantially.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts reduced oxidation weight gain and lower oxidation rate for ~10 at.% Al vs. lower-Al or uncoated baseline. The paper found a minimum in parabolic rate constant and oxygen penetration at ~10 at.% Al (Al-10) compared to Al-0 and higher-Al coatings. Both predict an optimum near 10 at.% Al with reduced oxidation, but the hypothesis does not capture the reversal at higher Al contents.
